title: MACH Software Entry
description: JSON Schema for MACH software entries (entries/software/*.jsonld). Status: DRAFT — not yet enforced in CI.

@context.description: Relative path to the MACH JSON-LD context file.

@id.description: Canonical IRI for this entry in the MACH catalog.

@type.description: schema.org type(s). Software entries use schema:SoftwareApplication and/or schema:SoftwareSourceCode.

identifier.description: Slug used as file name and internal key. Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens only.

alternateName.description: Abbreviations, former names, or alternate titles.

description.description: Rich editorial description. Should include: what it does, key features, language, license, stars, version, date, institutional origin, and notable publications.

url.description: Primary public URL (project site, docs, or GitHub if no separate site).

codeRepository.description: Source code repository URL (GitHub, GitLab, etc.).

relatedLink.description: Additional URLs: docs, PyPI, package registries, related projects.

license.description: SPDX license identifier (e.g. Apache-2.0, MIT, GPL-3.0, AGPL-3.0). Use LicenseRef-proprietary for non-OSI licences.

version.description: Most recent stable release version at time of editorial review.

dateModified.description: Date of the most recent release or significant commit (YYYY-MM-DD).

applicationCategory.description: schema.org applicationCategory. Use 'Healthcare' for all MACH entries unless a more specific term applies.

mach:category.description: Primary MACH taxonomy category. Software entries should use 'software'.

mach:governance.description: Who controls the project's direction and releases.

mach:deploymentContext.description: How the software is typically deployed.

mach:clinicalDomain.description: Clinical or research domains the software serves. Free-text for now; will be constrained to a controlled vocabulary in Phase 2.

mach:judgement.description: MACH editorial recommendation ring. Adopt=ready for production use; Assess=worth evaluating; Situational=right tool for specific contexts; Caution=significant barriers (license, maintenance, safety).

mach:judgementReason.description: 1–3 sentences explaining the judgement. Must address: evidence quality, maturity, license implications, and who should adopt/avoid.

mach:editorialReviewedAt.description: Date the entry was last substantively reviewed by a MACH editor (YYYY-MM-DD).

mach:evidence.description: Supporting evidence with at least one live primary-repo or documentation URL.

mach:swhid.description: Software Heritage persistent identifier for long-term archival.

_notes.status: DRAFT — open for review, not yet wired into CI validate.yml
open_questions: Should 'license' be validated against a known SPDX list or remain free-text?
Should mach:clinicalDomain be an enum now or stay free-text until Phase 2 classifier is built?
Should mach:swhid be required for Adopt-ring entries?
Minimum minLength for mach:judgementReason — 80 chars reasonable?
Should we add a maxLength for description to prevent runaway text?

standards_alignment.CodeMeta_3.0: name, description, url, codeRepository, license, version, programmingLanguage, operatingSystem, author, keywords map directly to CodeMeta terms
standards_alignment.schema.org: @type values (SoftwareApplication, SoftwareSourceCode) and applicationCategory follow schema.org
standards_alignment.mach_vocabulary: All mach: prefixed fields are defined in data/context/mach.jsonld
standards_alignment.SPDX_3.0: license field should use SPDX identifiers per SPDX 3.0 spec

next_steps: Create parallel schemas: models.draft.json, datasets.draft.json, mcp-servers.draft.json
Wire into CI validate.yml using ajv (Node) or jsonschema (Python)
Create SHACL shapes in data/shacl/ for RDF-level validation
Replace manual Python field checks in validate.yml once schemas are approved
